title: Possessive determiners
description: my, your, his, her, its, our, their – wem gehört was?
subject: Englisch

categories.name: Pronomen → Begleiter
categories.description: I → my, you → your, he → his …

questions.prompt: I have a dog. It's ___ dog.
You have a cat. It's ___ cat.
Ben has a bike. It's ___ bike.
questions.explanation: Ben ist ein Junge → his (sein).

questions.prompt: Emma has a guitar. It's ___ guitar.
questions.explanation: Emma ist ein Mädchen → her (ihr).

questions.prompt: The bird has a nest. It's ___ nest.
questions.explanation: Für Tiere und Dinge (it) heißt der Begleiter its – ohne Apostroph.

questions.prompt: We have a garden. It's ___ garden.
Tom and Lisa have a rabbit. It's ___ rabbit.
questions.explanation: Mehrere Besitzer (they) → their (ihr).

questions.prompt: You and Max have a new teacher. She's ___ teacher.
questions.explanation: your heißt dein, euer und Ihr – im Englischen immer dasselbe Wort.

questions.prompt: Which possessive determiner belongs to "they"?
Which possessive determiner belongs to "he"?
Sarah loves ___ new bike.
questions.explanation: his/her richtet sich nach der Person, der etwas gehört: Sarah → her.

questions.prompt: Jack can't find ___ PE bag.
questions.explanation: Jack ist ein Junge → his.

questions.prompt: Mr Green is our teacher. ___ car is red.
questions.explanation: Das Auto gehört Mr Green (Mann) → His.

questions.prompt: My grandma lives in York. ___ house is old.
questions.explanation: Das Haus gehört der Oma (Frau) → Her.

questions.prompt: Lucy is in Year 5. ___ favourite subject is Art.
Leon plays football. ___ team is very good.
Ergänze his oder her.
questions.text: Anna and {her} brother Max are at home. Max is playing with {his} computer.

questions.prompt: Ergänze his oder her.
questions.text: Dad is in the kitchen. {His} phone is on the table. Mum is looking for {her} keys.
questions.explanation: Dad → His, Mum → her. Entscheidend ist, wem etwas gehört.

questions.prompt: The dog is hungry. Give it ___ food, please.
questions.explanation: its = sein/ihr bei Tieren und Dingen. it's = it is.

questions.prompt: ___ a nice day today!
questions.explanation: It's = It is (Es ist). Der Apostroph steht für das fehlende i.

questions.prompt: Our school is big. ___ library has lots of books.
questions.explanation: Die Bücherei gehört der Schule (it) → Its. It's library = It is library ergibt keinen Sinn.

questions.prompt: Look at the cat! ___ playing with a ball.
questions.explanation: It's playing = It is playing.

questions.prompt: The bird is in ___ cage. (it)
questions.explanation: Der Käfig gehört dem Vogel (it) → its, ohne Apostroph.

questions.prompt: This is my rabbit. ___ name is Snowy. (it)
Schreibe its oder it's in die Lücken.
questions.text: {It's|It is} cold today, so the cat is in {its} basket.
questions.explanation: It's = It is. its = Besitz (der Korb der Katze).

questions.prompt: The tree in our garden is old. ___ leaves are yellow.
We love ___ new classroom.
The twins are at ___ grandparents' house.
questions.explanation: their = ihr (mehrere Besitzer). there = dort.

questions.prompt: Kids, put ___ books on the desk, please!
questions.explanation: Die Lehrerin spricht mehrere Kinder an: euer → your.

questions.prompt: Hi Emma! Is this ___ pencil case?
My friends and I have a club. ___ club meets on Fridays. (we)
Mr and Mrs Patel have two children. ___ children go to my school. (they)
questions.explanation: Mehrere Besitzer (Mr und Mrs Patel) → Their.

questions.prompt: Hello, Mr Brown! Is this ___ umbrella? (you)
questions.explanation: Auch die höfliche Form Ihr heißt im Englischen your.

questions.prompt: Ergänze die Begleiter.
questions.text: We often visit {our} aunt in London. The Smiths visit {their} cousins in York.

questions.prompt: Which English words can mean "ihr" or "Ihr"? Choose all.
questions.explanation: ihr Buch (von ihr) = her book, ihr Buch (von ihnen) = their book, Ihr Buch (höflich) = your book.

questions.text: This is {my} sister Mia. {Her} hobby is dancing.
Ben and I are friends. {Our} favourite game is chess. Ben's dog loves {its} ball.

questions.prompt: Schreibe die Begleiter in die Lücken.
questions.text: Can you help me? I can't find {my} pencil. Is it in {your} bag?
The children are in the park with {their} dog. {Its} name is Rocky.

questions.prompt: Schreibe die Begleiter in die Lücken.
questions.text: Is that Tom's jacket? – Yes, it's {his} jacket. Is that Lisa's bag? – Yes, it's {her} bag.

questions.prompt: Ich mag meinen Hund. → I like ___ dog.
Wo ist euer Klassenzimmer? → Where is ___ classroom?
questions.explanation: euer = your.

questions.prompt: Das ist ihr Haus. (Es gehört Paul und Lena.) → That's ___ house.
questions.explanation: Mehrere Besitzer → their.

questions.prompt: Das Pferd frisst sein Futter. → The horse eats ___ food.
questions.explanation: Bei Tieren und Dingen: its – auch wenn es im Deutschen „sein“ heißt.

questions.prompt: My brother and I have a cat. ___ cat is black.
___ my best friend, Noah!
questions.explanation: You're = You are (du bist). Your = dein/euer/Ihr.

questions.prompt: Is this ___ pencil case, Mia?
questions.explanation: Dein Mäppchen → Besitz → your.

questions.prompt: Du bist zu spät! → ___ late! (Kurzform)
questions.explanation: Du bist = you are → Kurzform you're (mit Apostroph).

questions.prompt: Euer Garten ist toll. → ___ garden is great.
questions.explanation: euer = your (Besitz, kein Apostroph).

questions.prompt: your oder you're?
questions.text: {You're} in my class, and {your} sister is in my brother's class.
questions.explanation: you're = you are; your = dein.

questions.prompt: Ergänze your oder you're.
questions.text: Mum, {you're} the best! Thanks for {your} help and {your} great cake.
questions.explanation: Vor einem Nomen steht your. you're heißt you are.

questions.prompt: Singular: Welcher Begleiter gehört zum Pronomen?
questions.explanation: I → my, you → your, he → his, she → her, it → its (ohne Apostroph).

questions.prompt: Plural: Welcher Begleiter gehört zum Pronomen?
questions.explanation: we → our, you → your (euer), they → their.
